candidates.summary: Android emulator side PCI + miscdevice driver with public out-of-tree C source and a strong fit for the current Rust PCI/miscdevice abstraction track.
candidates.expected_maintainer_context: Android virtualization / platform / miscdevice, not netdev.
candidates.oracle_strategy: Android emulator guest with adb-driven ABI tester, then differential oracle if guest/kernel alignment becomes tractable.
key_blockers: Requires Android emulator + adb environment before any runtime-equivalence claim.
Guest kernel alignment for true Rust-vs-C differential testing remains the highest-risk step.

candidates.summary: Real Android emulator driver with public source, but it crosses dma_fence/sync_file/IRQ/workqueue surfaces that are substantially larger than the current abstraction set.
candidates.oracle_strategy: Would also require Android emulator runtime plus a much larger in-kernel abstraction expansion.
key_blockers: Needs dma_fence, sync_file, IRQ, and workqueue abstractions.
Too much abstraction growth for the first non-net target.

candidates.summary: Real missing PHY driver with public source, but it falls back into Andrew/netdev review context and still depends on hardware-backed validation we do not currently have.
candidates.expected_maintainer_context: netdev/PHY, likely routed back to the same maintainer guidance that asked for real new hardware bring-up.
candidates.oracle_strategy: Requires real hardware or a convincing in-kernel differential harness because local VM-only testing is weak.
key_blockers: Would naturally re-enter the netdev review path we explicitly wanted to avoid for the next iteration.

candidates.summary: Excellent local oracle target for hardening the tool and runner stack, but weak as an upstream story because it does not map cleanly to a missing real-world driver request.
candidates.expected_maintainer_context: PCI/sample/testing rather than a strong new-driver submission path.
candidates.oracle_strategy: Standard QEMU device + local VM oracle; ideal for runner/family hardening, weaker for the first external-source upstream pitch.
key_blockers: Upstream narrative is weak compared with a real missing driver.
Better as a tool-hardening sample than a maintainer-facing flagship target.
